ARGUMENTS: Wayfinder ticket #86 "What is in and out of Release 2?" on map #85 (chrisdoc/surveybeat-next)

The ten Release 2 tickets are on map #85, and the AI research is running in the background. Here is the first round of decisions for #86, "What is in and out of Release 2?". The detailed rules belong to the later tickets (#88–#93); this round only sets the edges.

❓ **Q1 - Themes: who sees what.** Themes are generated when a Round closes, and only for Rounds that meet the minimum group size. The Lead sees the themes and still sees the redacted raw comments, as in Release 1. Members see the themes but never raw comments, which is SPEC §10's default.

➡️ Yes: themes for the Lead and members, raw comments for the Lead only.

---

❓ **Q2 - Redaction stays rule-based.** SPEC lists "comment redaction and themes" under Release 2, but Release 1 already redacts at store time with rules (ADR 0009). AI-assisted redaction would mean sending unredacted text to OpenRouter, names included.

➡️ Yes: no AI redaction. Only text that is already redacted ever leaves Cloudflare.

---

❓ **Q3 - AI is an Organization setting, off by default.** Sending comments to a third party is a new data flow. An Organization admin turns "AI themes" on. While it's off, themes and the AI parts of the discussion guide don't appear, and members are told in the answer flow whenever it's on.

➡️ Yes: off by default, switched on per Organization, disclosed to members.

---

❓ **Q4 - Discussion guide.** A short agenda for the Lead's team meeting:
- the biggest change, the lowest Dimension and open Actions, written by fixed rules;
- plus suggested questions written by the AI from the themes, only when AI is on.

Only the Lead sees it.

➡️ Yes: rules plus optional AI, Lead only.

---

❓ **Q5 - Team health overview.** One Team's Dimensions across all its Rounds, with markers showing when Actions were committed and completed. The Lead and members see it, just as both already see Results. There's no side-by-side view of several Teams; that's close to the Release 3 roll-ups.

➡️ Yes: one Team over time, no cross-Team view.

---

❓ **Q6 - Delayed sharing.** After a Round closes, the Lead has a review window before members see Results. Results go out when the Lead clicks "Share with the team", or automatically after 3 days. The Lead can't withhold Results indefinitely.

➡️ Yes: Lead review with an automatic share after 3 days.

---

❓ **Q7 - Private history page.** A member sees which Rounds they took part in. The server already knows that from Participation records, which store a Person but no answers. Their own past answers come only from their own browser, stored with the Edit key, so ADR 0005 is untouched. On a new device the answers are gone, and the page says so. Details go in #90.

➡️ Yes: browser-held answers only, no server-side link.

---

❓ **Q8 - German.** The app, the answer page and the emails all get German.
- Each Person can set their language; the default comes from the browser, then the Organization.
- I draft the translations and you review them.

➡️ Yes: everything in German, set per Person.

---

❓ **Q9 - Release 1 deferrals.** None of the items Release 1 deferred are pulled in: eNPS, multiple choice, the other three Templates, shared-link Distribution, other cadences, and so on. They stay out unless your first real Round shows a need.

➡️ Yes: none come along.

---

❓ **Q10 - First real Round.** Your team starts weekly Rounds early in Release 2, once the #94 checklist passes and before the Release 2 features land. Real comments then feed the work on themes and the discussion guide.

➡️ Yes: start early in Release 2, ahead of the Release 2 features.

The AI research for #87 is done and merged (PR #96, `docs/research/openrouter-muse-ember.md`). Its findings come from reading OpenRouter's docs and public APIs; no request was sent to the model. One result affects your choice of model:

**`meta/muse-ember` can't run without the provider keeping the data.**
- Meta is its only host. OpenRouter lists that host as keeping prompts for 30 days and not training on them, but not offering zero data retention.
- Asking OpenRouter for no retention (`zdr: true`) makes the request fail, because there's nowhere else to send it.
- Processing is in the US. The model isn't available through OpenRouter's EU routing.
- Meta's own terms don't say whether this model is in its no-training tier; only OpenRouter's label says it isn't used for training.
- OpenRouter's data processing agreement covers OpenRouter itself, not Meta's 30 days.

**What works well:**
- strict JSON-schema output;
- a 1-million-token context window;
- about $0.001–0.0025 per Round, which is an estimate until a real call measures it.

**Alternative:** `meta/muse-spark-open`, hosted on Together, Nebius or Modal, has zero-retention endpoints that OpenRouter can enforce on every request.

That adds one question to this round:

❓ **Q11 - Model given the retention finding.** Members' redacted comments are their own words. Keeping them for 30 days with a US provider, with unclear training terms, is a hard thing to explain on the answer page. "Trust before features" (SPEC §3.1) argues for enforced zero retention.

➡️ Yes: switch to `meta/muse-spark-open` with `zdr: true` enforced on every request, and keep OpenRouter. If you'd rather keep `muse-ember`, the ADR records the 30-day US retention, and members are told about it plainly before AI themes are switched on.

Both offer zero data retention (ZDR) through some of their hosts, at the same price as `muse-ember`. These figures come straight from OpenRouter's public API (`/models`, `/models/<id>/endpoints`, `/endpoints/zdr`).

**Price per million tokens and ZDR on OpenRouter**

| Model (OpenRouter id) | Price in / out | Hosts that offer ZDR | JSON-schema output |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openai/gpt-6-luna` (I took this to be "GPT Luna 6") | $0.10 / $0.50 | **Azure** only. OpenAI's own endpoints and Bedrock aren't on the ZDR list. | yes, on all hosts |
| `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` | $0.10 / $0.50 | **Google Vertex and Amazon Bedrock**. Anthropic direct, Claude Platform on AWS and Azure aren't on the ZDR list. | yes on Google; Bedrock lists only `response_format` |
| `meta/muse-ember` (your current pick) | $0.10 / $0.50 | **none**. Meta keeps prompts for 30 days. | yes |
| `meta/muse-spark-open` (my earlier suggestion) | $1.25 / $4.25 | Together, Nebius, Modal, Makora, BaseTen | yes, on most hosts |

**Cost per Round.** I assume one call per Round: 20 comments of about 300 characters plus instructions is about 2,000 input tokens, plus about 2,500 output tokens including the model's reasoning.
- **GPT-6 Luna, Haiku 5.5, Muse Ember:** about $0.0015 per Round, roughly 8 cents per Team per year of weekly Rounds.
- **Muse Spark Open:** about $0.013 per Round, roughly 70 cents per Team per year.

All four are negligible. The output figure is an estimate until a real call measures it.

**Updated recommendation for Q11:** use `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` with `provider: { zdr: true }` on every request. It costs the same as `muse-ember`, and OpenRouter can enforce zero retention. Requiring strict JSON-schema output as well would route requests to Google. GPT-6 Luna would also work, but only through Azure.

# Comments are redacted when stored, and the raw text is never kept

Release 1's rule-based redaction (ADR 0001) runs in the Submission Worker as the comment is saved. It uses the Organization's roster at that moment, and only the redacted text is stored. The raw text exists only in that request's memory. It is never logged, stored, or sent to a model. We rejected keeping the raw text and redacting each time a comment is shown, for two reasons. Deleting a Person would take their name out of the roster and expose it in every old comment that mentions them. And raw comments at rest would be the most identifying data SurveyBeat holds.

**What is removed:**
- first names, last names, full names, and email local parts of every Person in the Organization, matched as whole words, ignoring case, width, and accents (names shorter than 2 characters are ignored);
- email addresses, phone numbers (7 or more digits with common separators), @handles, and every URL.

Each match becomes a placeholder (`[name]`, `[email]`, `[phone]`, `[handle]`, `[link]`). A comment is never held back as a whole. Roster names that are also ordinary words ("will", "may") are redacted anyway.

## Consequences

- Redaction is permanent. A false positive can't be undone, and a member who edits their comment edits the redacted text.
- People added to the roster later are not redacted from older comments.
- No nicknames, no names outside the roster, and no "unusual identifying phrases" in Release 1. The answer page says exactly what is and isn't removed.
- The Release 2 AI pass can only ever run on new comments, because the raw text of older comments no longer exists.
## Resolution: Release 1 scope

Decided in a grilling session on 2026-11-07. Later tickets build against this list.

**In Release 1**

- **Question types:** rating (1–5, labeled ends), single choice, long text, and the optional "Want to say more?" comment on rating Questions. The Question type stays an open union.
- **Comments:** the Lead sees them only when the Round meets the minimum group size, after rule-based redaction (names from the Organization's roster, email addresses, phone numbers). The answer page says what the Lead will see. Members see no comments in R1. Recorded as ADR 0001 (`docs/adr/0001-r1-comments-rule-based-redaction.md`, on branch `t3/wayfinder-issue-1`).
- **Templates:** one Template, weekly team health, with Questions grouped into Dimensions (workload, psychological safety, clarity, recognition).
- **Changing Questions:** a Lead can remove, reorder, and add Questions (from the Template or newly written, which creates the first Question version). A Question that has Answers cannot be edited. Question version is modelled from day one, with exactly one version per Question in R1. The pulse editor shows an estimated answer time and warns above 7 Questions or about 90 seconds.
- **Distribution:** Invitation only. Distribution is modelled and fixed per Pulse.
- **Cadence:** weekly only, at a day and time in each member's local time zone. Cadence is modelled so other rules can be added later.
- **Lead controls:** skip a Scheduled Round, pause and resume a Pulse, close an Open Round early, cancel an Open Round.
- **Answer window and reminders:** the answer window is 1–6 days (default 3). The Lead picks 0, 1, or 2 reminders (default 1) at fixed points in the window. Reminders go only to members without a Participation record.
- **Reminder opt-out:** a one-click POST (RFC 8058, List-Unsubscribe) applies per Person per Pulse. Members cannot opt out of Invitations; the Lead ends the Membership instead.
- **Anonymity mode:** anonymous only. The field exists with one allowed value.
- **Changing a Submission:** members can change answers until the Round closes, via the Edit key. This uses the same mechanism as the one-tap flow.
- **Member view of Results:** after AuthKit sign-in, members see the same Results page as the Lead, without comments. In R1, Ready moves straight to Shared; both states stay in the model. A results-ready email goes to the Lead and members. Answering never needs sign-in; viewing Results always does.
- **Actions:** only the Lead creates Actions, from a Result. Each Action has a title, an owner (a Person in the Team), an optional due date, a link to the Result, and an optional Dimension. Statuses are committed, done, and dropped. Proposed is modelled but unused.
- **Where Actions appear:** the next Invitation email and the thank-you screen, at most three: those still committed, plus those marked done since the previous Round.
- **Organization shape:** several Teams with no nesting. Roles are lead and member; viewer is modelled but unused. Each Pulse belongs to one Team, and there are no cross-Team views.

**Not in Release 1:** eNPS, multiple choice, short text, the typo-vs-meaning Question editor, the onboarding, sprint retro, and manager feedback Templates, shared-link Distribution, cadences other than weekly, one-off surveys, attributed and confidential modes, member-proposed Actions, Action follow-up questions, the member's private history page, delayed sharing, and Team nesting and the viewer role.

**Flag for later:** the manager feedback Template scores one Person (the Lead), which is close to SPEC §9. Raise it as a scope question before it is scheduled.

# Comment themes use Claude Haiku 5.5 through OpenRouter, with zero data retention, in the EU, switched on per Organization

Release 2's AI features (comment themes and the AI part of the discussion guide) call `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` through OpenRouter. Every request sets `provider.zdr: true`, is pinned to the two zero-data-retention endpoints that run in the EU (`google-vertex/europe`, then `amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1`), and allows no fallback. If neither endpoint can serve the request, it fails and is retried later; it never leaves the EU or goes to an endpoint that keeps data. This replaces SPEC §10 question 4's default (Workers AI only), chosen by the product owner on 2026-11-10 (map #85).

**What is sent:** only comment text that rule-based redaction has already processed (ADR 0009), and the Question text. Never a name, a Person id, a Membership, a Round id, a Team or Organization name, a time, or anything that links a comment to a Submission (ADR 0005). The Organization Durable Object makes the call with a key held as a Worker secret, a timeout, and retries that honour `Retry-After`. Response and error bodies are never logged, because a provider's moderation error can echo comment text.

**Off by default.** An Organization admin turns AI processing on for the Organization. While it is off, nothing is sent and the AI features do not appear. While it is on, the answer page and the Invitation say plainly that redacted comments are processed by an AI service in the EU that keeps nothing.

**Request shape** (Chat Completions):

```json
{
  "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
  "provider": {
    "zdr": true,
    "only": ["google-vertex/europe", "amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1"],
    "order": ["google-vertex/europe", "amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1"],
    "allow_fallbacks": false,
    "data_collection": "deny"
  },
  "response_format": { "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": { "strict": true } },
  "max_tokens": 2000
}
```

The OpenRouter account also has prompt and output logging off, "use of inputs/outputs" off, and a dedicated key whose guardrail allows only this model, enforces ZDR, and caps spend.

## Considered options

- **`meta/muse-ember`** (the first choice): no zero-retention endpoint exists. Meta, its only host, keeps prompts for 30 days, is not on EU routing, and its own terms don't say whether this model is trained on. Rejected: members' words would sit with a US provider for 30 days ([research note](../research/openrouter-muse-ember.md)).
- **`openai/gpt-6-luna`:** same price, zero retention only through Azure. Viable, but Haiku 5.5 has EU zero-retention endpoints with strict JSON-schema output.
- **`meta/muse-spark-open`:** zero retention on several hosts, but about 9× the price, with no advantage over Haiku 5.5.
- **Workers AI** (SPEC's default): keeps everything inside Cloudflare, but the product owner chose OpenRouter.

## Consequences

- Cost is about $0.0015 per Round ($0.10 per million input and $0.50 per million output tokens; one call of about 2,000 input and 2,500 output tokens), an estimate until a real call measures it.
- OpenRouter is a sub-processor (its DPA is part of its terms), and so are Google Cloud or AWS for the model call. Customer-facing privacy pages must name them.
- OpenRouter's account and abuse-monitoring metadata may be processed in the US even when the model call runs in the EU. Comment text is not part of that metadata under ZDR.
- If either EU endpoint drops ZDR or leaves OpenRouter, requests fail closed rather than going elsewhere. A test asserts the request body above.

Read `gh issue view 93`, map #85 (`gh issue view 85`), the scope decision comment on #86 (German for app, answer page, and emails; language per Person, defaulting to the browser, then the Organization; translations drafted by Claude and reviewed by the product owner), AGENTS.md, docs/adr/0008-workspace-layout-and-toolchain.md (answer page budget: JS ≤ 10 KB gzip critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB, HTML ≤ 8 KB; it currently has ~1 KB JS headroom), and the code: apps/web/src/messages/ (catalog.ts, index.ts, messages.test.ts), packages/emails/src/messages/, how the answer page loads messages (apps/web/vite.config.ts prerenderAnswer, apps/web/src/answer/main.ts, the messages-*.js chunk), the lint rule no-literal-ui-text in tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat, and where a Person record lives (packages/domain/src/people, Organization Durable Object) for a language preference. Existing research notes live in docs/research/ — match their style.

Answer, citing code paths and primary docs (MDN/ECMA-402 for Intl, HTML lang, Accept-Language), and measuring where possible:
1. Catalog shape for a second locale: keep TypeScript catalogs (`de` object typed as `Record<keyof typeof en, string>` so a missing key fails typecheck) vs JSON; plural rules for de (Intl.PluralRules), dates/numbers (Intl), the `{placeholder}` checks staying compile-time.
2. Locale choice: Person setting stored where, fallback to Accept-Language / navigator.language, then Organization default; how emails pick the recipient's locale (the Queue consumer renders per recipient).
3. Answer page within budget: measure current gzip of the critical JS and the messages chunk (build with `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build`), and propose how to load only one locale (e.g. per-locale messages chunk chosen by an inline head script from the token response or navigator.language) — estimate the byte cost and whether a second prerendered answer.html per locale is better. Note that the answer page knows no Person before the token exchange.
4. HTML `lang`, `<title>` empty rule (messages.test.ts), and tests that check every key exists in both catalogs.
5. Translation workflow: Claude drafts, owner reviews in PR; glossary terms in German (Pulse, Round, Lead, Team, Submission, Organization) — propose German renderings and whether product nouns stay English.
Do NOT change production code. Write findings to `docs/research/german-localization.md` with a short answer first. Commit on a new branch `t3/wayfinder-issue-93` from origin/main (if that local branch name exists, use `t3/wayfinder-issue-93-research`), push (if the push is rejected without a reason, retry once), open a PR titled "Research: German localization (#93)" with body "Part of #85. Findings for #93." ending with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)", squash-merge it, delete the remote branch. End the commit message with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>". Do not close #93 or edit the map. Report a 6–10 line summary (recommended catalog shape, locale choice, answer-page approach with measured byte cost, glossary German renderings, risks) and the PR URL.

I've closed #86, the Release 2 scope ticket, with your answers recorded on it. ADR 0015 is merged (PR #97). It records Claude Haiku 5.5 through OpenRouter:
- zero data retention enforced on every request;
- requests pinned to the EU hosts `google-vertex/europe` and `amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1`, with no fallback;
- only redacted text sent;
- off by default for each Organization.

That also closed #87, and map #85 lists both decisions.

The German research (#93) is running in the background: <t3-thread://v2/461d8aa0-9e53-4578-a3c9-db2468bbeda5/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A7aa672c1-afe7-48cf-bcf1-28859b62d109%3Adelegate-task%3A7c0fa534-c846-4c96-95f4-9dd42ed38bda>.

Next round of decisions, covering #88 (themes), #89 (delayed sharing), #90 (history page) and #91 (overview):

❓ **Q1 - Theme shape.** At most 5 themes per Round. Each has a short label and a one-sentence summary written in neutral words. No counts are shown to members; the Lead sees how many comments support each theme.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **Q2 - A theme needs at least 2 comments.** A theme built from a single comment is that one person's words, reworded, shown to the whole Team. Comments that fit no theme with 2 or more supporters stay visible only to the Lead, as raw comments.

➡️ Yes: at least 2 comments per theme.

---

❓ **Q3 - No quotes in themes.** Themes paraphrase and never quote a comment word for word, because exact wording or a personal style can identify the author.

➡️ Yes: no quotes. The prompt and the JSON schema enforce it, and a check rejects any theme that repeats 6 or more words of a comment in a row.

---

❓ **Q4 - When themes fail or arrive late.** Themes are computed once, after the Round closes, and stored in the Organization's Durable Object. If the call fails, it retries with backoff for up to 24 hours. Meanwhile Results show "Themes are being prepared". If it still fails after that, Results go out without themes. Delayed sharing never waits on themes.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **Q5 - The Lead can't edit or hide themes.** Letting the Lead hide an unflattering theme before sharing would undercut "trust before features". The Lead can only add context in the discussion.

➡️ Yes: themes are shown exactly as generated.

---

❓ **Q6 - Review window is set per Pulse.** It's a Pulse setting from 0 to 7 days, default 3. Zero means Results are shared immediately, as in Release 1.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **Q7 - What members see during review.** The Results page says "Your Lead is reviewing these Results. They'll be shared by {date}." The results-ready email goes to members when Results are shared, and to the Lead at close.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **Q8 - Private history page.** For each Round the member took part in, it shows their own answer from this browser next to the Team's shared score. That only appears once Results are shared and above the minimum group size. Browser-stored answers are kept for 1 year, and the member can clear them.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **Q9 - Where the overview lives.** The Team page becomes the overview: one trend line per Dimension across all Rounds, plus Action markers. Lead and members see the same page. The Question-level detail stays on each Round's Results page.

➡️ Yes.

While you answer, I'll work through the #94 checklist myself: WorkOS sign-in methods, the allowlist, the production email test and the deploy state.

I tested this with the repo's `tsc`: a missing key, an extra key, or a misspelt `{placeholder}` each fails typecheck. The format doesn't change, so no ADR is needed for it. German plurals use the same `one`/`other` forms as English, and dates and numbers come from `Intl` once the hard-coded `LOCALE = "en"` becomes a parameter.
- **Choosing the language:**
  - **App:** add nullable `person.locale` and `person.detected_locale`, plus `organization.default_locale`, in the Organization Durable Object. The order is the Person's setting, then the browser (`navigator.languages`), then the Organization.
  - **Emails:** the Durable Object works out the language when it creates the send and stores it in `StoredEmail`. The Queue consumer renders with it and sets `<Html lang>`.
- **Answer page:** I measured the current critical path at 9,243 B gzip of the 10,240 B budget: 4,057 B for `answer.js` and 5,186 B for the shared `messages` chunk, which holds all 269 keys but the page uses 27. Adding German to that chunk would bring it to about 14.4 KB, over budget.
  - **Recommendation:** prerender one page per language (`/a` and `/de/a`), each loading only its own answer catalog: 756 B gzip for English, 831 B for my German draft. That brings the critical path to an estimated 5.2 KB.
  - The answer page knows no Person before the token exchange, but the email is rendered for one known recipient, so its link can pick the page.
  - This beats choosing a catalog in a head script, which would flash English text and add a request.
- **Glossary in German:** Pulse and Team stay English; Round → Runde, Lead → Teamleitung, Organization → Organisation, Submission → Einsendung. I suggest the informal *du*. The product owner decides these when reviewing.
- **Risks:**
  - The delivery-time and unsubscribe pages in `MainWorker.ts` have hard-coded English and `lang="en"`, and the lint rule doesn't check that package.
  - The Template's Question text is English and gets copied into each Pulse, so a German team would see English Questions.
  - `budget.test.ts` has to be rewritten per page before the split, or it stops checking the real files.
  - The language must never be stored with a Submission: in a small Team it could identify the one German reader.
  - Redaction has no test cases for German phone number formats.

95:| `production` | Sends through Cloudflare Email Sending from `team@notify.surveybeat.app` | The `notify.surveybeat.app` sending subdomain, the `send_email` binding, the `EmailEvents` queue, and its event subscription |
96:| `pr-<n>`, personal, `test_*` | Renders the message and records it in the stage's D1 table `captured_email`. Sends nothing. | No sending subdomain, no `send_email` binding, no event subscription |
98:The sending subdomain makes Cloudflare create its DKIM, SPF, DMARC, MX, and bounce records under `notify.surveybeat.app`. Nothing at the apex changes: its SPF, DMARC, MX, and mail-server records belong to the existing mail setup and are not managed by Alchemy. Message previews in the Cloudflare activity log are off (`previewEnabled: false`), because messages will carry Invitation links.
106:No stage other than `production` can send real mail. To try real sending elsewhere, change `sendsRealEmail` in `packages/cloudflare/src/Email.ts` on a throwaway branch and deploy a personal stage. That stage then also claims `notify.surveybeat.app` and its event subscription, so destroy it before production is deployed.
108:**Send states.** `pending → sending → sent | failed(reason)`. A delivery takes a two-minute lease before calling the provider, and the call times out after 30 seconds. A clear rejection (`E_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and other coded errors) returns the send to `pending` and the message is retried after 30 s, 60 s, and 120 s; the fourth rejection fails it. Permanent rejections (`E_RECIPIENT_SUPPRESSED`, sender and header errors) fail at once. An error without a code, a timeout, or a lease that expired with no outcome fails the send as `unknown`, and it is never resent automatically. A message the queue dead-letters fails its send too (`abandoned`, or `rejected` after earlier rejections).
110:**Bounces and complaints.** Alchemy's `Cloudflare.Queues.Subscription` with the `email.sending` source subscribes the `EmailEvents` queue to `message.bounced`, `message.complained`, `message.rejected`, and `message.failed` for the sending subdomain. The consumer finds the send through the D1 table `email_message` (provider message id → Organization and send) and fails it with the event's reason.
112:**Fallback.** Postmark would be a second `EmailSender` adapter in `packages/cloudflare`, with its webhooks parsed into the same delivery events (`docs/research/cloudflare-email-sending.md` §9). It is not built.

## Understanding and acting

**Result**:
The derived, recomputable aggregate of a closed Round: scores, response rate, and Comment themes.
_Avoid_: Report, analytics, stats

**Typical change**:
How much a Team's score for one Question or Dimension usually moves from one Round to the next, judged from the Team's own history. A change well beyond it is shown as larger than usual.
_Avoid_: Significance, noise threshold, variance

**Redaction**:
Replacing names of the Organization's People, contact details, handles, and links in a comment with placeholders before anyone can read it.
_Avoid_: Anonymization, scrubbing, masking

**Comment theme**:
A machine-written summary of a group of comments, with a label, sentiment, count, and redacted quotes.
_Avoid_: Cluster, topic, insight

**Action**:
A commitment the Team makes in response to a Result, with an owner, a due date, and a status.
_Avoid_: Action item, task, todo

**Note**:
The Lead's free-text summary of a team discussion, visible to the Team.
_Avoid_: Comment (that is free text in an Answer)

cat > docs/adr/0016-comment-themes.md <<'EOF'
# Comment themes are computed once at close, need two comments, never quote, and can't be edited

When a Round closes and meets the minimum group size, and the Organization has AI processing on (ADR 0015), the Organization Durable Object asks the model for at most 5 Comment themes over the Round's redacted comments (ADR 0009). Each theme is a short label and one neutral sentence. The model also returns which comments support each theme, and the object keeps only themes supported by **at least two comments**. The result is stored with the Round's Result and never recomputed.

**Who sees what.** Members see each theme's label and sentence, never raw comments and never counts. The Lead sees the themes, how many comments support each, and the redacted raw comments, as in Release 1. Comments that fit no theme with two supporters stay visible only to the Lead.

**No quotes.** The prompt and the JSON schema ask for paraphrase, and a check rejects any theme that repeats 6 or more consecutive words of a comment; a rejected theme is dropped, not repaired. Exact wording or a personal style can identify the author.

**Failure.** The call retries with backoff for up to 24 hours. Until it succeeds, Results show "Themes are being prepared"; after that, Results stand without themes. The Review window (#89) never waits for themes.

**No editing.** The Lead cannot edit, hide, or reorder themes. A Lead who could hide an unflattering theme before sharing would undercut trust before features (SPEC §3.1).

## Considered options

- **Themes from a single comment:** rejected. Shown to the whole Team, a one-comment theme is one person's words in other words.
- **Redacted quotes under each theme** (the old glossary wording): rejected for the same reason as quotes in the sentence.
- **Recomputing themes on view:** rejected. It would call the model on every view, could change what people already saw, and needs the comments sent again.

## Consequences

# A member's history page reads past answers only from their own browser

The member's private history page lists the Rounds the member took part in, from their Participation records, which the server already holds with a Person and no answers (ADR 0005). Their own past answers come only from their own browser: when the answer page saves a Submission, it also keeps the member's answers in local storage next to the Edit key, for one year, and the member can clear them. For each Round the page shows the member's own answer beside the Team's score, but only once the Result is shared and the aggregate meets the minimum group size.

The server never learns which Submission is the member's. A new device or cleared browser data shows the Rounds without answers, and the page says why.

## Considered options

- **Server-side history encrypted with a key only the member holds:** rejected for Release 2. Key recovery across devices is hard to get right, and any server-side record of a member's answers, encrypted or not, weakens the A1–A10 invariants (ADR 0005) that the privacy suite proves.
- **Only the Team's Results the member took part in, no own answers:** too little to be worth a page.

## Consequences

- Answers stay on one device. The page must state this plainly.
- Comments are kept in the browser as the member typed them, not redacted; they never leave the device.
- Clearing site data or a private window loses the history. Nothing on the server can restore it.
EOF

# German ships as typed catalogs per locale, a prerendered answer page per locale, and a bilingual Template

Release 2 adds German to the app, the answer page, and emails ([research](../research/german-localization.md)).

- **Answer page:** one prerendered page per locale (`/a`, `/de/a`), each loading only its own answer catalog. The Invitation link picks the page from the recipient's language. ADR 0008's budget applies to each page separately.
- **Words:** informal "du". Pulse and Team stay English; Round → Runde, Lead → Teamleitung, Organization → Organisation, Submission → Einsendung. Claude drafts, the product owner reviews in the PR.
- **Template:** the weekly team health Template ships in both languages; a new Pulse copies its Questions in the Lead's language. Existing Pulses keep their Questions.
- **Privacy:** the language is never stored with a Submission or an Answer. In a small Team it could single out the one German reader.

## Consequences

- The budget test runs per answer page.
- Pages rendered in `MainWorker.ts` (delivery time, unsubscribe) hold hard-coded English and must move to the catalog.
- Redaction gains German phone number cases.

I've closed #88–#91 and #93 and updated map #85. ADRs 0016–0018 and the glossary are merged in PR #99:
- **0016 Comment themes:** at least 2 comments per theme, no quotes, and the Lead can't edit or hide them.

Two tickets are left before slicing: #92 (discussion guide), and #94 (first-Round checklist), which is waiting on you. I'll stop slicing from waiting on #94, since the first Round can run alongside implementation. Here's the #92 round:

❓ **Q1 - Guide contents.** Four short sections:
1. "What stood out": Dimensions with a bigger change than usual, and the lowest-scoring Dimension, by rules.
2. "What people raised": the themes, when AI is on.
3. "Actions to check on": committed Actions and their owners.
4. "Questions to ask": 3 open questions.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **Q2 - AI questions come from themes and scores only.** They're written in the same model call as the themes, from the themes and Dimension changes, never from raw comments. They never mention a person or guess who said what. The JSON schema allows at most 3.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **Q3 - Without AI, questions come from a fixed set.** Each Dimension and direction has prepared questions in the catalog (in German too). For example, when workload drops: "What made this week's workload hard to manage?"

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **Q4 - Where it appears.** A "Discussion guide" panel on the Results page, visible only to the Lead, during and after the Review window, with a "Copy as text" button for meeting notes.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **Q5 - Add the Note.** The glossary already defines a Note: the Lead's free-text summary of the team discussion, visible to the Team. Proposal: the guide ends with a Note field the Lead fills in after the meeting, shown to members on the Results page. It closes the loop between discussion and Actions, at small cost.

➡️ Yes: include the Note in Release 2.

# The discussion guide is written by the AI, in the same call as the themes, for the Lead only

When a Round closes and meets the minimum group size, and the Organization has AI processing on (ADR 0015), the call that writes the Comment themes (ADR 0016) also writes the Round's discussion guide. It has four sections: what stood out, what people raised, Actions to check on, and at most 3 questions to ask the Team. A Round without comments still gets a guide from its scores and Actions.

**Input.** This extends ADR 0015's list of what may be sent: the Dimension scores and changes (with which are flagged as larger than usual), the redacted comments, the Question text, and the titles of open Actions passed through the same Redaction (ADR 0009). Never an Action owner, a Person, or any name, id, or time.

**Rules.** The guide never quotes (the 6-word-run check of ADR 0016 applies to every section), never says or guesses who said what, and must match a strict JSON schema. A guide that fails a check is dropped as a whole.

**No AI, no guide.** There is no rule-based fallback. With AI processing off, the Lead sees a line saying an Organization admin can turn it on. If the call fails for 24 hours, the Round has no guide.

**Lead only, as generated.** The guide is stored with the Result, generated once, shown only to the Lead on the Results page with a "Copy as text" button, and cannot be edited in SurveyBeat. After the conversation, the Lead can write a Note on the Results page that the Team sees.

## Considered options

- **Rules-written guide with optional AI questions:** rejected by the product owner; the guide is the AI's job.
- **A separate call for the guide:** rejected; it would send the comments twice.

- The guide exists only for Organizations that turn AI processing on, and only for Rounds that close afterwards.
- The privacy rule table gains rows for the guide: never below N, never shown to members, never containing a 6-word run from a comment, never naming an Action owner.

content.text:
Release 2 planning is finished, and Release 1 is closed.

**Release 1:** #83 (summary sentence) and #84 (dark mode) are merged, so every slice is done. I closed #34 with a note pointing to Release 2.

**Release 2 map (#85):** every decision is recorded.

| Ticket | Decision |
|---|---|
| #86 Scope | Themes, an AI-written discussion guide, the Team overview, delayed sharing, the history page and German. None of Release 1's deferred features. The first real Round starts early in Release 2. |
| #87 AI provider (ADR 0015) | Claude Haiku 5.5 through OpenRouter. Requests run only on EU hosts that keep no data, with no fallback. Only redacted text is sent, and AI is off by default for each Organization. |
| #88 Themes (ADR 0016) | At most 5, each backed by at least 2 comments, never quoting a comment. The Lead can't edit them. |
| #89 Delayed sharing | A Review window of 0–7 days per Pulse (default 3). The Lead shares Results, or they're shared automatically when it ends. |
| #90 History page (ADR 0017) | Past answers are read only from the member's own browser. |
| #91 Overview | The Team page shows Dimension trends with Action markers. |
| #92 Discussion guide (ADR 0019) | Written by the AI in the same call as themes, for the Lead only, with no fallback when AI is off. The Lead writes a Note the Team sees. |
| #93 German (ADR 0018) | A German text file per catalog, one answer page per language, the informal "du", and a bilingual Template. |

**Implementation: [Release 2: implementation](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/101), 10 slices**
- AI chain: **#102** AI setting and OpenRouter client → **#103** themes and guide computed at close → **#104** both shown on Results.
- German chain: **#109** catalogs and language choice → **#110** German answer page, and **#111** bilingual Template plus German phone-number redaction.
- Independent: **#105** Lead's Note, **#106** Review window, **#107** Team overview, **#108** history page.

**Still waiting on you (#94)**
- Confirm a sign-in method is enabled in WorkOS Production (sign in at app.surveybeat.app).
- An email deliverability check with your team.
- Create your Team and Pulse, then the first Round.

Six slices can start now: #102, #105, #106, #107, #108 and #109. I'd start with #102, since the AI features depend on it, and run #106 (Review window) in parallel because it touches different files. Should I begin?
